auraIntro: Explorer, Whirlpool Galaxy is the textbook example of a grand design spiral galaxy, interacting with companion NGC 5195.
overview: The Whirlpool Galaxy (M51a or NGC 5194) is an iconic grand design spiral galaxy located 23 million light-years away in the constellation Canes Venatici.
formation: Its distinct double spiral structure is driven by gravitational tidal encounters with smaller dwarf companion NGC 5195.
structure: A grand design spiral galaxy spanning 76,000 light-years, featuring sweeping spiral arms enriched with bright pink H II starbirth regions.
discoveryHistory: Discovered on October 13, 1773 by Charles Messier. Its spiral structure was first drawn in 1845 by Lord Rosse.
observationTips: A favorite for amateur astronomers; 4-inch telescopes reveal its companion galaxy, while 8-inch instruments show sweeping spiral arms under dark skies.
funFacts: First celestial object ever identified as possessing a spiral structure (by Lord Rosse using the 'Leviathan of Parsonstown' in 1845).
Tidal compression from companion galaxy NGC 5195 triggers massive waves of newborn star formation along its arms.
Multiple supernovae have been observed in M51 over recent decades, including SN 1994I, SN 2005cs, and SN 2011dh.

cards.title: Gravitational Tidal Engine
cards.subtitle: NGC 5195 Interaction & Starburst Waves
cards.body: Gravitational tides from dwarf galaxy NGC 5195 compress gas in M51's disk, igniting thousands of bright blue young star clusters.
bulletPoints: First spiral structure drawn in astronomical history (1845).
Companion NGC 5195 passed through M51's disk ~500 million years ago.
JWST MIRI observations reveal intricate dust filament networks.
